questions.stem: What do we know about this year's Nobel prizes from the news report?
options: A) The three researchers shared evenly the Nobel prize.
B) The three winners studied the same subject.
C) This year's first Nobel prize was awarded for medicine.
D) All of the Nobel prizes have been made public.

explain.定位:
The first of this year's Nobel prizes has been awarded for medicine, and it has gone to three
researchers for work against parasitic diseases.
今年第一个诺贝尔奖已颁发给医学领域，授予了三位研究者，以表彰他们在抗寄生虫病方面
的工作。
explain.信号:
新闻首句点题，顺听即得。新闻报道把最核心的事实放在开篇第一句 The first of this
year's Nobel prizes has been awarded for medicine，"first""medicine"两个关键事实在
此一并交代，这就是答案信号——新闻首句即题眼。
explain.替换:
The first of this year's Nobel prizes has been awarded for medicine ↔
This year's first Nobel prize was awarded for medicine
几乎原句对应，仅语序微调
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 借了原文真出现的 three researchers，听到"三个人"就想选；但原文说 one half jointly
to William C. Campbell and Satoshi Omura…the other half to Youyou Tu，是"两人共
得一半、屠呦呦独得另一半"，并非 shared evenly（三人平分），细节对不上。
借用原文：one half jointly to William C. Campbell and Satoshi Omura for their discoveries
concerning a novel therapy against infections caused by roundworm parasites and the other half to
Youyou Tu
B) 与原文相反
B 用了"三位获奖者"这个真事实诱你，但原文明确分成两组课题：坎贝尔和大村智研究
infections caused by roundworm parasites（蛔虫感染），屠呦呦研究 a novel therapy
against malaria（疟疾），并非 studied the same subject，与原文相反。
借用原文：one half jointly to William C. Campbell and Satoshi Omura for their discoveries
concerning a novel therapy against infections caused by roundworm parasites and the other half to
Youyou Tu for her discoveries concerning a novel therapy against malaria
D) 过度推断
D 盗用了 Nobel prizes 这个词，但原文从头到尾只讲 The first of this year's Nobel
prizes——第一个奖刚公布，根本没说"全部"奖项都已公开，All of the Nobel prizes have
been made public 把范围从"一个"夸成"全部"。
借用原文：The first of this year's Nobel prizes has been awarded for medicine

questions.stem: How is Youyou Tu's treatment different from Campbell and Omura's?
options: A) Youyou Tu's treatment is more hi-tech.
B) Youyou Tu's treatment is more traditional.
C) Youyou Tu focuses on roundworm-caused infections.
D) Youyou Tu invented a completely new therapy.

explain.定位:
As a Chinese woman working in China, and using traditional Chinese medical records,
she rediscovered an ancient plant-based treatment for malaria that worked where
modern therapies failed. Campbell and Omura's was a more hi-tech approach against the
debilitating roundworm.
作为一位在中国工作的中国女性，她借助传统中医药记录，重新发现了一种古老的、基于植
物的疟疾疗法，在现代疗法失效的地方它却奏效。而坎贝尔和大村智的则是一种更偏高科技
的方法，针对的是使人衰弱的蛔虫。
explain.信号:
对比落点，前后两句一传统一高科技。答案信号是这处显性对比：屠呦呦那句用 traditional
Chinese medical records、an ancient plant-based treatment，紧接着 Campbell and
Omura's was a more hi-tech approach 把另一组定为"高科技"，两句一前一后摆出"传统
vs 高科技"，正是问差别处。
explain.替换:
using traditional Chinese medical records, she rediscovered an ancient plant-based treatment ↔
Youyou Tu's treatment is more traditional
传统中医/古老植物疗法概括为 more traditional
Campbell and Omura's was a more hi-tech approach ↔
Youyou Tu's treatment is more traditional
对方是高科技，反衬屠呦呦更传统
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
A 借了原文真念过的 more hi-tech 勾人下手，但原文这个词是贴给 Campbell and
Omura's 的，不是屠呦呦的；把对方的"高科技"安到屠呦呦头上，正是张冠李戴。
借用原文：Campbell and Omura's was a more hi-tech approach against the debilitating roundworm
C) 张冠李戴
C 搬来原文真出现的 roundworm 制造熟悉感，但原文里蛔虫属于 Campbell and
Omura's…approach against the debilitating roundworm，屠呦呦研究的是 a novel
therapy against malaria（疟疾）；把蛔虫感染安给屠呦呦，是张冠李戴。
借用原文：Campbell and Omura's was a more hi-tech approach against the debilitating roundworm
D) 与原文相反
D 蹭了原文 novel therapy 给人"新疗法"的印象，但原文说屠呦呦是 she rediscovered an
ancient plant-based treatment——重新发现一种古老疗法，而非 invented a
completely new therapy（发明全新疗法）；"rediscover ancient"与"invent completely
new"方向正相反。
借用原文：she rediscovered an ancient plant-based treatment for malaria that worked where
modern therapies failed
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 "Under certain circumstances, liquid water has been found on Mars." This was the out of this world
announcement from NASA following years of exploration on the Red Planet. Scientists revealed salty
water may flow on the planet's surface during its summer months. Different soil samples were found to
be moist and full of water. Dark streaks, known as recurring slope lineae, or RSL, are now known to
have been caused by flowing water. "These discoveries are very important, but they were only part of
the hydrological cycle on Mars that we are just now beginning to understand. What we are going to
announce today is that Mars is not that dry planet we thought of in the past." So what does this tell us
about potential life on Mars? Exploration by the Curiosity Rover proves that billions of years ago it was
once a planet similar to Earth. But could the planet support life today? Scientists say, technologically, we
will now be able to answer those questions.

questions.stem: What does the news report mainly discuss?
options: A) NASA sent a new Mars lander.
B) Different soil samples were studied.
C) Scientists revealed a new space theory.
D) Liquid water has been found on Mars.

explain.定位:
"Under certain circumstances, liquid water has been found on Mars." This was the out of this
world announcement from NASA following years of exploration on the Red Planet.
"在特定条件下，火星上已发现液态水。"这就是 NASA 经过多年对这颗红色星球的探索后所
作的惊世宣布。
explain.信号:
开篇首句即点题 + announcement 一词标明这是新闻主旨。新闻惯于开篇第一句就抛核
心；这里首句直接是 liquid water has been found on Mars，紧接着用 announcement
from NASA 点明这正是本则新闻要宣布的事，开头点题就是主旨信号。
explain.替换:
liquid water has been found on Mars ↔ Liquid water has been found on Mars.
本题正确项罕见地几乎原句复现，但仍要靠"它是开篇主旨句"来定
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
NASA sent a new Mars lander. 盗用了录音里反复出现的 announcement from NASA 中
的 NASA 和 Mars，听到这两个熟词容易顺手选；但录音通篇没说"发射 / 派出新着陆器"，
属听到原词就误选。
借用原文：announcement from NASA
B) 原词陷阱
Different soil samples were studied. 几乎照搬录音 Different soil samples were found
to be moist，听到原词极想选；但"土壤样本"只是支撑"有水"的一个细节，本题问 mainly
discuss，细节当不了主旨。
借用原文：Different soil samples were found to be moist
C) 偷换概念
Scientists revealed a new space theory. 借用了录音里 Scientists revealed 这个动作，但
录音 reveal 的是"咸水可能流动"这一发现，不是"new space theory（新太空理论）"，
把"实物发现"偷换成了"理论"。
借用原文：Scientists revealed salty water may flow

questions.stem: What are scientists going to announce today, according to the news?
options: A) Mars is not as dry as what we used to think.
B) Mars could support life at the moment.
C) They have found living things on Mars.
D) Soil samples from Mars are the same as those of the Earth.

explain.定位:
What we are going to announce today is that Mars is not that dry planet we thought of in
the past.
我们今天要宣布的是：火星并不是我们过去所认为的那颗干燥星球。
explain.信号:
强调结构 What we are going to announce today is… 直接框出答案。What we are
going to announce today is that 与题干 announce today 完全对应，is 后面那句就是要
宣布的内容；这种"What…is that…"强调句把答案明明白白框出来，是最硬的定位信号。
explain.替换:
Mars is not that dry planet we thought of in the past ↔
Mars is not as dry as what we used to think
同义改写：not that dry…in the past = not as dry as…used to think
explain.排除:
B) 过度推断
Mars could support life at the moment. 把录音 could the planet support life today?
这个"疑问"当成了"结论"，还把待解的问题说成 at the moment（此刻）就能——录音说的
是"今天还能不能维持生命"是个待答之问，不是要宣布的内容。
借用原文：But could the planet support life today?
C) 过度推断
They have found living things on Mars. 借录音反复出现的"火星 / 生命"话题，把"找到
水"夸大成"找到生物（living things）"；录音只说发现液态水、火星曾像地球，从未说找到
任何生命体。
借用原文：So what does this tell us about potential life on Mars?
D) 原词陷阱
Soil samples from Mars are the same as those of the Earth. 盗用了录音 Different soil
samples 和 a planet similar to Earth 的熟词；但录音说的是"火星曾经与地球相似"，绝
非"土壤样本与地球完全相同（the same as）"，把 similar（相似）偷换成 same（相
同），且嫁接到 soil 上。
借用原文：it was once a planet similar to Earth

questions.stem: By whom was the woman victim shot?

explain.定位:
A Florida gun-rights supporter remained in the hospital Friday three days after she was shot
by her 4-year-old son.
一名佛罗里达州的持枪权支持者周五仍在住院，三天前她被自己 4 岁的儿子开枪打伤。
explain.信号:
新闻首句即点核心事实。新闻报道惯于在第一句把"谁、被谁、怎么了"一次说清，本则正是
开篇就给出 she was shot by her 4-year-old son；信号就是"被动语态 was shot by +
人"这个结构，by 后面那个人就是开枪者。
explain.替换:
she was shot by her 4-year-old son ↔ Her 4-year-old son.
by后人物即答案
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
全篇没有 kidnapper（绑匪）这个词，也无任何绑架情节；A kidnapper. 是凭"枪击案"常识
脑补出来的，属无中生有。
B) 未提及
录音没有提到任何 rival（对手/情敌）；Her rival. 同样是想象"枪击"背后有恩怨纠纷，原文
毫无依据。
D) 张冠李戴
录音确实念到了 harm me or my family 里的 family，且后文出现 victim 等词，容易让人
脑补出"丈夫"；但全篇真正和"开枪"绑定的只有 4-year-old son，Her drunken husband.
里的"醉酒丈夫"录音根本没说，是张冠李戴式的诱饵。

questions.stem: From Gilt's message on the Facebook page, what can we conclude?
options: A) She is brutal in nature.
B) She is a die-hard racist.
C) She loves shooting and killing.
D) She is a firm gun-rights supporter.

explain.定位:
A Facebook page, listed under Gilt's name, included this message one day before Tuesday's
shooting: "If someone breaks into my house, or tries to harm me or my family pretty
anywhere, they will be shot and most likely killed. It's my right to protect my life."
一个登记在 Gilt 名下的 Facebook 页面，在周二枪击案前一天发布了这样一段话："如果有
人闯进我家，或在任何地方试图伤害我或我的家人，他们会被开枪打死，而且很可能丧命。
保护自己的生命是我的权利。"
explain.信号:
她原话里的"权利"表态。答案信号是她本人引语里那句 It's my right to protect my life
——"开枪自卫是我的权利"这种强调用枪权利的措辞，正是判断她立场的落点；推断题要抓
说话人亲口表态的关键句，而非旁人转述。
explain.替换:
It's my right to protect my life ↔ She is a firm gun-rights supporter.
强调用枪权=拥枪派
they will be shot and most likely killed ↔ firm gun-rights supporter
坚决用枪→firm
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
她说 they will be shot and most likely killed，是针对"闯入伤害家人"的自卫表态，She is
brutal in nature.（生性残暴）却把它拔高成对她整个人的性格定性，推过了头。
借用原文：they will be shot and most likely killed
B) 未提及
She is a die-hard racist.（顽固种族主义者）涉及种族立场，而录音从头到尾只字未提种
族，纯属凭空安插。
C) 原词陷阱
录音里有 they will be shot and most likely killed，选项 She loves shooting and
killing.（热爱开枪杀戮）正是盗用 shot、killed 这两个原词，把"自卫时会用枪"歪曲成"以
杀戮为乐"，听到原词就想选就会中招。
借用原文：they will be shot and most likely killed

questions.stem: What was said about Florida law according to the news?
options: A) It is against the law to own a gun.
B) Women are not allowed to possess a gun.
C) Improper storing of guns constitutes a crime.
D) All the citizens have the right to carry a gun.

explain.定位:
Florida law makes it a crime to store a loaded weapon in such a way that it can be taken or
used by a child, according to the sheriff's department.
据治安官部门称，佛罗里达州法律规定：以致儿童能够取得或使用的方式存放已上膛的枪
支，构成犯罪。
explain.信号:
law makes it a crime 的明示规定。信号是关键词 law 后紧跟的 makes it a crime to
store a loaded weapon——"使……成为犯罪"这种明示法律后果的措辞，正是法律细节题
的答案句；锁 law 这个词，它后面就是规定内容。
explain.替换:
makes it a crime to store a loaded weapon in such a way that it can be taken or used by a child ↔
Improper storing of guns constitutes a crime.
不当存枪=犯罪
makes it a crime ↔ constitutes a crime
make a crime=constitute a crime
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
录音说的是"不当 store（存放）"枪才犯罪，It is against the law to own a gun. 却
说"own（拥有）枪本身违法"——录音从没说拥枪违法，只是把违法对象从"存放方式"偷换
成了"拥有"。
借用原文：store a loaded weapon
B) 未提及
新闻主角恰是位女性（the woman victim），易让人误以为法律针对女性；但 Women
are not allowed to possess a gun.（女性不得持枪）在录音里毫无依据，法律针对的
是"存放方式"，与性别无关。
D) 原词陷阱
录音里 right 一词出现在她个人引语 It's my right to protect my life 中，All the citizens
have the right to carry a gun. 盗用 right 并夸大成"所有公民都有携枪权"，既偷换了主体
（她个人→all citizens），也把"自卫的权利"偷换成"携枪的权利"，原文并未如此规定。
借用原文：It's my right to protect my life

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: A) He likes Sweden better than England.
B) He prefers hot weather to cold weather.
C) He is an Englishman living in Sweden.
D) He visits London nearly every winter.

explain.定位:
Swedish people always complain that when they visit England, the houses are cold even in a
good winter.
瑞典人总抱怨说，他们去英格兰时，那里的房子即使在不太冷的冬天也很冷。
explain.信号:
全程自述 + 开头 "I live in Sweden" 定身份。男士开口就是 When I say I live in
Sweden，自报 "我住在瑞典"；通篇又把英格兰称作 much warmer than at home（"比家
里暖和"，即他老家在英格兰），两处合起来锁定 "英国人、现住瑞典" 这一身份。这是 "说
话人自述" 的信号——身份题盯第一人称的自我交代。
explain.替换:
I live in Sweden ↔ living in Sweden
I live → living，同一事实换说法
much warmer than at home ↔ an Englishman
at home（指英格兰）→ Englishman，隐含推导
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
他客观讲了瑞典冬冷夏好，也提了伦敦，但从没说 "更喜欢瑞典甚于英格兰"；He likes
Sweden better than England. 是把 "住在瑞典" 强行升级成 "偏爱瑞典"，原文没有这层偏
好比较。
B) 原词陷阱
录音反复出现 it is cold, very cold in winter、warm 等冷暖词，He prefers hot weather
to cold weather. 借这些词编出 "他偏好热天"，可他通篇都在赞美瑞典夏天的长昼，从没表
达过 "偏爱炎热、讨厌寒冷" 的个人偏好。
借用原文：it is cold, very cold in winter
D) 原词陷阱
录音末尾提到 Londoners work longer hours，出现 London 与全篇的 winter，He visits
London nearly every winter. 就把这些词拼成 "几乎每个冬天都去伦敦"，但录音从没讲他
造访伦敦的频率，nearly every 是凭空夸大。
借用原文：Londoners work longer hours

questions.stem: What do Swedish people complain about when they visit England in winter?

explain.定位:
Swedish people always complain that when they visit England, the houses are cold even in a
good winter.
瑞典人总抱怨说，他们去英格兰时，那里的房子即使在不太冷的冬天也很冷。
explain.信号:
抱怨动词 complain 直接引出对象。答案句里 complain 这个词正是题干用词，它后面紧跟
的 the houses are cold 就是抱怨的具体对象。这是 "题干动词在原文原样出现、其后宾语
即答案" 的信号——听到题问的那个动词，记牢它后面跟的名词。
explain.替换:
the houses are cold ↔ The cold houses.
句子→名词短语，同一信息浓缩
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
瑞典人抱怨的是英格兰的 houses are cold（房子冷），不是泛泛的天气坏；The bad
weather. 是个更大的帽子词，把具体对象偷换成了模糊的大概念，答非所问。
借用原文：the houses are cold even in a good winter
B) 原词陷阱
同段确实念到 even in a good winter，The gloomy winter. 就借 winter 这个词把抱怨对
象引到 "阴沉的冬天"，但瑞典人抱怨的是房子冷，不是冬天阴沉；况且 gloomy（阴沉）描
述的是后文的黑暗，不是这里的话题。
借用原文：even in a good winter
D) 张冠李戴
录音后文确有 around Christmas time there's only one hour of daylight 讲长夜，The
long night. 借这个真话题冒充答案，但那是男士在讲瑞典的黑暗、和 "瑞典人去英格兰抱怨
什么" 是两码事，对象与场景都不对。
借用原文：there's only one hour of daylight

questions.stem: How does the man describe the short hour of daylight around Christmas in Sweden?

explain.定位:
Well, yeah, around Christmas time there's only one hour of daylight, so you really look
forward to the spring. It is sometimes a bit depressing.
嗯，是啊，圣诞前后每天只有一个小时的日光，所以你会特别盼着春天到来。这有时是有点
令人压抑的。
explain.信号:
评价句 It is ... depressing 直接给感受。他先客观说 only one hour of daylight，紧接一
句 It is sometimes a bit depressing——用评价性形容词 depressing 直接亮出感受。这
是态度题的信号：客观描述之后那句 "It is + 形容词" 才是他的真实评价。
explain.替换:
depressing ↔ Depressing.
评价词原样落到选项
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
他形容白昼极短是 a bit depressing（有点压抑），Delightful. 是愉悦正面，极性正好反
了；delightful 那种愉悦他是用来形容夏天长昼的，不是圣诞的短昼。
借用原文：It is sometimes a bit depressing
B) 过度推断
他只说 a bit depressing（有点压抑），程度很轻；Painful. 是 "痛苦"，负面方向虽对，但
程度被夸大到痛苦，与 "a bit"（有点）的轻描淡写不符。
借用原文：a bit depressing
D) 与原文相反
Refreshing.（清新提神）是正面感受，和他对短昼的 depressing 负面评价方向相反；
refreshing 更贴近他对夏天的描述，挪到这里极性就错了。
借用原文：It is sometimes a bit depressing

questions.stem: What does the man say about the Swedish people?
options: A) They often stay up late reading.
B) They work hard and play hard.
C) They like to go camping in summer.
D) They try to earn more and spend more.

explain.定位:
Often they start work earlier in summer and then leave at about 2 or 3 in the afternoon, so that
they can really enjoy the long summer evenings. They'd like to work hard, but play hard, too.
夏天他们常常更早开始工作，然后下午两三点就下班，好让自己尽情享受漫长的夏夜。他们
想努力工作，但也想尽情玩乐。
explain.信号:
总评句 work hard, but play hard 收束。前面铺垫他们夏天早上班、早下班去享受夏夜，
最后一句 work hard, but play hard, too 是对这群人的总结性评价。这是 "具体行为之后的
概括句" 信号——一串描述末尾那句对仗总评，往往就是答案。
explain.替换:
work hard, but play hard, too ↔ They work hard and play hard.
but…too 改为 and，意思不变
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 read a newspaper 和 stay up all night 确实出现过 read 和 stay up，They often
stay up late reading. 就把这两词拼成 "常熬夜读书"，但原文说的是夏夜亮到午夜还能看
报，不是 "瑞典人有熬夜读书的习惯"，把偶发现象说成日常习惯。
借用原文：You want to stay up all night
C) 原词陷阱
录音多次讲 the summers are amazing，They like to go camping in summer. 借
summer 这个真话题冒充答案，但 "露营 camping" 录音从头到尾没出现过，是凭空添加的
活动。
借用原文：the summers are amazing
D) 未提及
They try to earn more and spend more. 故意做成和 They work hard and play hard. 一
样的 "X more and Y more" 对仗，迷惑你凭节奏选；但录音讲的是 work hard / play hard
（努力与玩乐），从没提 "多赚多花"，钱的话题是无中生有。

questions.stem: What was the man's major at university?

explain.定位:
Well, I did a degree in French at Nottingham.
嗯，我在诺丁汉大学读的是法语学位。
explain.信号:
被问者的直接应答。女士先问背景，男士开口第一句 I did a degree in French at
Nottingham 就是对『学什么专业』的正面回答——对话题里被问方应答的第一句往往就是
答案落点。
explain.替换:
a degree in French ↔ French.
同一专业的展开与缩写
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
English literature 确在录音出现，但那是女士自述 I did an English literature degree，被
安到男士头上就错了——这是把甲的话记到乙账上的典型。
借用原文：I did an English literature degree
B) 原词陷阱
录音确有 management，但出现在 training courses in management techniques（谈培
训课程内容），不是男士的专业，听到 management 就选 B 即落陷阱。
借用原文：training courses in management techniques
D) 原词陷阱
administration 在录音里指男士后来转去做的行政方向 more interested in the
administrative side，且他明说当年没有这种学位，把它当专业即误选。
借用原文：more interested in the administrative side

questions.stem: What was the man's job in secondary schools?

explain.定位:
After that, I did careers work in secondary schools like the careers guidance people here at
the university.
在那之后，我在中学做就业指导工作，就像我们大学里这些做就业指导的人一样。
explain.信号:
自述动词 + 限定场景双重命中。男士用 I did careers work in secondary schools，既有
自述动词 did，又出现题干限定词 secondary schools，两条线在这句交汇，正是答案句。
explain.替换:
careers work in secondary schools like the careers guidance people ↔ Careers guidance.
同义改写 careers work = careers guidance
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
English teaching 在录音中并无对应——女士有 English literature 学位，但那是专业不是
教学工作，男士也没做过英语教学，属凭印象捏造。
B) 原词陷阱
training 确被念到，但在 plenty of training courses in management techniques，说的
是现在可参加的培训课程，不是男士在中学的岗位，听到 training 就选 B 即中招。
借用原文：plenty of training courses in management techniques
D) 未提及
Psychological counselling 录音从未出现，careers guidance（就业指导）与
psychological counselling（心理咨询）是两回事，不能因都带『指导/咨询』味就混选。

questions.stem: What does the woman share in common with the man?
options: A) They went to the same university.
B) They all love to engage in management.
C) The jobs they choose are not related to their major.
D) They received the same job training.

explain.定位:
Well, I know in my case, I did an English literature degree and I didn't really expect to end up
doing what I'm doing now.
嗯，就我自己来说，我读的是英国文学学位，可我真没想到最后会做现在这份工作。
explain.信号:
女士自陈与男士境遇呼应。女士说自己 did an English literature degree 却 didn't really
expect to end up doing what I'm doing now，呼应男士前面专业是 French、工作却转
做行政——两人都是专业与工作不对口，交集就此浮现。
explain.替换:
I did an English literature degree and I didn't really expect to end up doing what I'm doing now ↔
The jobs they choose are not related to their major.
具体叙述概括为『专业与工作不对口』
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
男士读 Nottingham，女士只说自己读 English literature、未说同校；后文男士还交代来
自 the north of England, from West Yorkshire，并无『同一所大学』的依据，same
university 站不住。
借用原文：the north of England, from West Yorkshire
B) 过度推断
录音提到男士对 administrative side 感兴趣，但从未说女士也热爱管理，更没说『两人都
爱』，由片面信息推全体属过度引申。
借用原文：more interested in the administrative side
D) 原词陷阱
training 在录音里指 training courses in management techniques，是泛指可参加的课
程，录音从没说两人受过『同样的职业培训』，借 same job training 制造共同点纯属拼
凑。
借用原文：training courses in management techniques

questions.stem: What attracted the man to Nottingham University?

explain.定位:
Nottingham was one of the universities I put on my list. And I like the look of it. The campus
is just beautiful.
诺丁汉是我列入名单的大学之一。我喜欢它的样子，校园实在太美了。
explain.信号:
本人表态句 I like… 加强调。男士亲口说 I like the look of it 并强调 The campus is just
beautiful，用 just 加重语气点名了吸引点——表态句正是这类题的答案信号。
explain.替换:
The campus is just beautiful ↔ Its pleasant environment.
beautiful campus 概括为 pleasant environment
explain.排除:
A) 未提及 scholarships 在录音中完全没出现，男士谈的是校园外观，奖学金属凭空添加。
B) 过度推断
诺丁汉虽是知名大学，但男士说选它是因为 I like the look of it、校园漂亮，从没说被『世
界声誉』吸引；这是凭『名校该因名气吸引人』的常识硬填，最迷惑也最该警惕。
C) 原词陷阱
courses 确被念到，但在 plenty of training courses in management techniques（谈培
训课程），与他选诺丁汉的理由无关，听到 courses 就联想 well-designed courses 即误
选。
借用原文：plenty of training courses in management techniques

questions.stem: What did Obcamp's speech focus on?
options: B) Some features of Japanese culture.
C) The art of Japanese brush painting.
D) The uniqueness of Japanese art.

explain.定位:
While Gail Obcamp, an American artist, was giving a speech on the art of Japanese brush
painting to an audience that included visitors from Japan, she was confused to see that many
of her Japanese listeners had their eyes closed.
美国艺术家盖尔·奥布坎普正在做一场关于日本毛笔画艺术的演讲，听众里有来自日本的访
客，这时她困惑地发现，许多日本听众都闭着眼睛。
explain.信号:
开头点题句·a speech on…。答案落在开头一句的 a speech on the art of Japanese
brush painting 上：篇章独白常在第一句就交代‘谁在讲什么’，giving a speech on the art
of Japanese brush painting 直接点出演讲主题，是典型的开头点题信号。
explain.替换:
a speech on the art of Japanese brush painting ↔ The art of Japanese brush painting.
几乎原句搬到选项
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音说 Gail Obcamp 是 an American artist（一位美国艺术家），选项 Characteristics of
Japanese artists. 借 artist 这个原词，把话题偷换成‘日本艺术家的特征’；可录音讲的是‘毛
笔画这门艺术’，不是艺术家有什么特征，听到 artist 就选会中招。
借用原文：Gail Obcamp, an American artist
B) 偷换概念
录音确实多次提到日本文化、文化差异，Some features of Japanese culture. 借了
culture 这层意思，但‘日本文化的一些特征’范围太宽——演讲聚焦的是‘毛笔画艺术’这件具
体事，文化只是后文延伸的背景，拿它当主题就以偏概全反过来说成‘过宽’了。
借用原文：the art of Japanese brush painting
D) 未提及
The uniqueness of Japanese art. 说‘日本艺术的独特性’，可录音从头到尾只是交代演讲主
题、再讲听众反应，从没比较或强调日本艺术‘独一无二’，uniqueness 这个意思原文根本没
出现，属凭空添加。

questions.stem: Why do Japanese listeners sometimes close their eyes while listening to a speech?
options: D) To signal lack of interest.

explain.定位:
Obcamp later found out that her listeners were not being disrespectful. Japanese listeners
sometimes close their eyes to enhance concentration.
奥布坎普后来发现，她的听众并不是不尊重她。日本听众有时闭上眼睛是为了增强专注力。
explain.信号:
先否定误解·再 to 给真因。答案靠两个信号锁定：先用否定 were not being disrespectful
推翻‘不尊重’的误会，紧接着用 to enhance concentration 这个 to + 动词的目的结构给出
真正原因——‘先否定误解、后给真因’的句式，落点永远在后半。
explain.替换:
to enhance concentration ↔ To enhance concentration.
目的结构原样对应
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
To calm themselves down. 说‘让自己冷静下来’，原文给的原因只有‘增强专注’，从没提闭
眼是为了平复情绪，calm 这层意思原文没有，是凭空补的合理化解释。
C) 与原文相反
To show their impatience.（表示不耐烦）正是录音要推翻的负面误解那一类。原文明说
were not being disrespectful、还讲他们是 showing their respect，闭眼是尊重不是不耐
烦，选 C 等于取了被否定掉的反面。
借用原文：her listeners were not being disrespectful
D) 原词陷阱
录音里出现过 signal（Were they deliberately trying to signal their rejection），To
signal lack of interest. 借这个原词，又把意思引向‘表示没兴趣’；可那句 signal 是演讲者
最初的疑虑、随后被否定，闭眼根本不是表示没兴趣，听到 signal 就选会上当。
借用原文：trying to signal their rejection of her

questions.stem: What does the speaker try to explain?
options: A) How listeners in different cultures show respect.
B) How speakers can win approval from the audience.
C) How speakers can misunderstand the audience.
D) How different Western and Eastern art forms are.

explain.定位:
Learning how different cultures signal respect can help you avoid misunderstandings.
了解不同文化如何表达尊重，能帮你避免误解。
explain.信号:
段末总结句·主旨落点。答案落在第一段结尾的总结句 Learning how different cultures
signal respect can help you avoid misunderstandings：它由前面‘闭眼’的例子收束上
来，是说话人点明意图的句子；第二段又用 deaf culture、whistling 等更多例子来支撑‘不
同文化表达尊重的方式不同’，开头例子+结尾总结+二段补例三处合起来，主旨就是‘不同文
化的听众如何表达尊重’。
explain.替换:
how different cultures signal respect ↔ How listeners in different cultures show respect.
signal=show 的同义替换
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
第二段提到 whistling… is a sign of approval，How speakers can win approval from
the audience. 借 approval 这个原词，又把主语改成 speakers‘如何赢得听众赞许’；可全
段讲的是‘听众如何表达尊重’，主体是听众不是演讲者，方向被偷换。
借用原文：whistling by listeners is a sign of approval
C) 原词陷阱
原文结尾说了解文化能 help you avoid misunderstandings，How speakers can
misunderstand the audience. 借 misunderstand 这个原词，却说成‘演讲者如何误解听
众’；原文落点是‘避免误解’，且开头是演讲者误解听众的反面例子、主旨是教人避免它，不
是讲‘如何误解’。
借用原文：can help you avoid misunderstandings
D) 原词陷阱
录音开头提到日本毛笔画这门艺术（art），How different Western and Eastern art
forms are. 借 art 这个原词，把话题拉到‘东西方艺术形式有多不同’；可全段讲的是不同文
化里听众怎样表达尊重，从没比较东西方艺术形式，方向跑偏。
借用原文：the art of Japanese brush painting

questions.stem: What is Chris's main responsibility at Taxalong Company?
options: C) Drawing up plans for in-service training.

explain.定位:
Chris is in charge of purchasing and maintaining equipment in his division at
Taxalong Company.
Chris 负责在他所在分部采购和维护设备。
explain.信号:
表"负责"的标志词 in charge of。录音开头第一句 Chris is in charge of purchasing and
maintaining equipment 用 in charge of 直接点出职责，这类"负责"标志词后面跟的就是
答案，是细节题最稳的定位信号。
explain.替换:
purchasing and maintaining equipment ↔ Buying and maintaining equipment.
purchasing 同义替换为 Buying
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里确有 evaluation interview 和 personnel director，A 项 Directing personnel
evaluation 把这两个原词拼在一起，听着耳熟；但原文是说 Chris 要去"接受"评估面谈，不
是说他"主管"人事评估，盗词却答非所问。
借用原文：an evaluation interview with his supervisor and the personnel director
C) 原词陷阱
录音提到 Chris began a program to train employees，C 项 Drawing up plans for in-
service training 借了 train／training 这个原词；但那是他做过的一项改进，不是他在公司
的"主要职责"，问的是 main responsibility，C 答非所问。
借用原文：Chris began a program to train employees to use equipment better
D) 原词陷阱
录音说 Two employees that Chris hired were stealing，D 项 Interviewing and
recruiting employees 借了 employees、hired 的影子（recruit≈hire）；但"招过两个员
工"是顺带提到的事，并非他的"主要职责"，仍属答非所问。
借用原文：Two employees that Chris hired were stealing

questions.stem: What problem did Chris encounter in his division?
options: A) Some of his equipment was damaged in a fire.
B) The training program he ran was a failure.
C) Two of his workers were injured at work.
D) Two of his employees committed theft.

explain.定位:
Unfortunately, one serious problem developed during the year. Two employees that Chris
hired were stealing, and he had to fire them.
不幸的是，这一年里出了一个严重问题。Chris 雇的两名员工偷东西，他不得不把他们解
雇了。
explain.信号:
麻烦信号词 Unfortunately＋problem。录音用 Unfortunately, one serious problem
developed 主动预告负面落点，紧接的 Two employees that Chris hired were stealing
就是这个 problem 的具体内容，是"信号词+下一句"的标准答案结构。
explain.替换:
Two employees that Chris hired were stealing ↔ Two of his employees committed theft.
stealing 名词化为 committed theft
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 he had to fire them 的 fire 是"解雇"，A 项 damaged in a fire 借 fire 字面玩"火
灾"的歧义来钓人；但原文 fire 此处是"开除"，根本没提任何火灾，属与原文无关的捏造。
借用原文：he had to fire them
B) 与原文相反
录音说培训 The training saved time for the employees and money for the
company，是好事；B 项却说 The training program he ran was a failure（培训失
败），借 training 原词把方向彻底说反，与原文相反。
借用原文：The training saved time for the employees and money for the company
C) 偷换概念
录音确有 Two employees，C 项 Two of his workers were injured at work 借"两个人"的
数字和 workers≈employees，把事件从"偷窃"偷换成"工伤"；原文从没提受伤，属偷换概
念。
借用原文：Two employees that Chris hired were stealing

questions.stem: What does Chris hope for in the near future?
options: A) A better relationship with his boss.
B) Advancement to a higher position.
C) A better-paying job in another company.
D) Improvement in the company's management.

explain.定位:
Chris knows that a new job for a purchasing and maintenance manager for the whole
company will be opened in a few months, and he would like to be promoted to the job.
Chris 知道几个月后全公司将开放一个采购与维护经理的新职位，他很想被提拔到这个职
位上。
explain.信号:
意愿信号 would like to be promoted。录音用 he would like to be promoted to the
job 直接表达意愿，would like to 是"想要"的标志词，其后 be promoted 就是他盼望的目
标，是表期望类细节题的核心定位信号。
explain.替换:
he would like to be promoted to the job ↔ Advancement to a higher position.
be promoted 名词化为 Advancement
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音后文有 his boss likes Kim's work 提到 boss，A 项 A better relationship with his
boss 借 boss 原词编出"想搞好与老板关系"；但原文只说老板喜欢 Kim 的工作，从没说
Chris 盼望改善与老板的关系，属未提及。
借用原文：his boss likes Kim's work
C) 偷换概念
录音说新职位是 for the whole company 内部晋升，C 项 A better-paying job in
another company 借 job、company 的影子，把方向偷换成"去别的公司拿高薪"；原文是
想在本公司内升职，不是跳槽，属偷换概念。
借用原文：a new job for a purchasing and maintenance manager for the whole company
D) 过度推断
录音里 manager、maintenance 频出，D 项 Improvement in the company's
management 借 management 的近形词，把 Chris 的个人升职愿望拔高成"改善公司管
理"；原文从没说他盼望公司管理变好，属过度推断。
借用原文：a new job for a purchasing and maintenance manager

questions.stem: What do we learn about Kim from the passage?
options: A) She has more self-confidence than Chris.
B) She works with Chris in the same division.
C) She has more management experience than Chris.
D) She is competing with Chris for the new job.

explain.定位:
Chris knows, however, that someone else wants the new job, too. Kim is in charge of
purchasing and maintenance in another division of the company.
然而 Chris 知道，还有别人也想要这个新职位。Kim 负责公司另一个分部的采购与维护
工作。
explain.信号:
转折 however＋someone else wants…too。录音用 however, that someone else
wants the new job, too 引出第二个竞争者，however 提示语义转折、someone else 引
入新人物，紧接点名 Kim，说明 Kim 与 Chris 在争同一职位，是"转折引新人物"的关键
信号。
explain.替换:
someone else wants the new job, too ↔ She is competing with Chris for the new job.
也想要同一职位＝竞争关系
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
录音从没把 Kim 与 Chris 在"自信"上作比较，A 项 She has more self-confidence than

B) 与原文相反
录音明说 Kim 在 another division of the company（另一个分部），B 项 She works
with Chris in the same division 借 division 原词却说成"同一部门"，与原文 another（不
同）相反。
借用原文：Kim is in charge of purchasing and maintenance in another division of the company
C) 过度推断
录音说 Kim has also made several changes over the year（也做了若干改进），C 项
She has more management experience than Chris 借管理类词把它编成"管理经验比
Chris 多"；原文只说两人都做了改进、要被比较，从没说谁经验更多，属过度推断。
借用原文：She has also made several changes over the year

questions.stem: Why are proverbs so important?
options: A) They help us see the important values of a culture.
B) They guide us in handling human relationships.
C) They help us express ourselves more effectively.
D) They are an infinite source of human knowledge.

explain.定位:
Many proverbs remind people of the values that are important in the culture.
许多谚语让人们想起在该文化中重要的价值观。
explain.信号:
话题词 values 集中出现处即功能陈述句。录音在 Many proverbs remind people of the
values that are important in the culture. 这句把 proverbs 与 values 直接挂钩，正是预
读锁定的话题词集中处；它正面陈述谚语的功能（让人记起文化中重要的价值观），是承载
答案的功能句。
explain.替换:

questions.stem: Some professionals in education are collecting signatures to voice their opposition to automated essay grading.

And then, instead of being done with that exam, imagine that the system would immediately let you rewrite the test to try to improve your grade.

B) EdX, the nonprofit enterprise founded by Harvard and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) to offer courses on the Internet, has just introduced such a system and will make its automated(自动的) software available free on the Web to any institution that wants to use it. The software uses artificial intelligence to grade student essays and short written answers, freeing professors for other tasks.

C) The new service will bring the educational consortium(联盟) into a growing conflict over the role of automation in education. Although automated grading systems for multiple-choice and true-false tests are now widespread, the use of artificial intelligence technology to grade essay answers has not yet received widespread acceptance by educators and has many critics.

D) Anant Agarwal, an electrical engineer who is president of EdX, predicted that the instant-grading software would be a useful teaching tool, enabling students to take tests and write essays over and over and improve the quality of their answers. He said the technology would offer distinct advantages over the traditional classroom system, where students often wait days or weeks for grades. "There is a huge value in learning with instant feedback," Dr. Agarwal said. "Students are telling us they learn much better with instant feedback."

One longtime critic, Les Perelman, has drawn national attention several times for putting together nonsense essays that have fooled software grading programs into giving high marks. He has also been highly critical of studies claiming that the software compares well to human graders.

The group, which calls itself Professionals Against Machine Scoring of Student Essays in High-Stakes Assessment, has collected nearly 2,000 signatures, including some from famous people like Noam Chomsky.

They cannot measure the essentials of effective written communication: accuracy, reasoning, adequacy of evidence, good sense, ethical(伦理的) position, convincing argument, meaningful organization, and clarity, among others."

It offers free online classes from Harvard, MIT and the University of California-Berkeley; this fall, it will add classes from Wellesley, Georgetown and the University of Texas. In all, 12 universities participate in EdX, which offers certificates for course completion and has said that it plans to continue to expand next year, including adding international schools.

I) The EdX assessment tool requires human teachers, or graders, to first grade 100 essays or essay questions. L) Two start-ups, Coursera and Udacity, recently founded by Stanford faculty members to create "massive open online courses," or MOOCs, are also committed to automated assessment systems because of the value of instant feedback. "It allows students to get immediate feedback on their work, so that learning turns into a game, with students naturally(吸引) drawn toward resubmitting the work until they get it right," said Daphne Koller, a computer scientist and a founder of Coursera.

M) Last year the Hewlett Foundation, a grant-making organization set up by one of the Hewlett-Packard founders and his wife, sponsored two $100,000 prizes aimed at improving software that grades essays and short answers. More than 150 teams entered each category. A winner of one of the Hewlett contests, Vik Paruchuri, was hired by EdX to help design its assessment software.

N) "One of our focuses is to help kids learn how to think critically," said Victor Vuchic, a program officer at the Hewlett Foundation. "It's probably impossible to do that with multiple-choice tests. The challenge is that this requires human graders, and so they cost a lot more and they take a lot more time."

O) Mark D. Shermis, a professor at the University of Akron in Ohio, supervised the Hewlett Foundation's contest on automated essay scoring and wrote a paper about the experiment. In his view, the technology—though imperfect—has a place in educational settings.

P) With increasingly large classes, it is impossible for most teachers to give students meaningful feedback on writing assignments, he said. Plus, he noted, critics of the technology have tended to come from the nation's best universities, where the level of teaching is much better than at most schools.

Q) "Often they come from very famous institutions where, in fact, they do a much better job of providing feedback than a machine ever could," Dr. Shermis said. "There seems to be a lack of appreciation of what is actually going on in the real world."

questions.stem: The author believes that a single-sex school would_______.
options: A) Force boys to hide their emotions to be "real men"
B) Help to cultivate masculine aggressiveness in boys
C) Encourage boys to express their emotions more freely
D) Naturally reinforce in boys the traditional image of a man
questions.passage:
Boys' schools are the perfect place to teach young men to express their emotions and involve them in activities such as art, dance and music.

Far from the traditional image of a culture of aggressive masculinity(阳刚), the absence of girls gives boys the chance to develop without pressure to conform to a stereotype, a US study says.

Boys at single-sex schools were said to be more likely to get involved in cultural and artistic activities that helped develop their emotional expressiveness, rather than feeling they had to conform to the "boy code" of hiding their emotions to be a "real man".

The findings of the study go against received wisdom that boys do better when taught alongside girls.

Tony Little, headmaster of Eton, warned that boys were being failed by the British education system because it had become too focused on girls. He criticised teachers for failing to recognise that boys are actually more emotional than girls.

The research argued that boys often perform badly in mixed schools because they become discouraged when their female peers do better earlier in speaking and reading skills.

But in single-sex schools teachers can tailor lessons to boys' learning style, letting them move around the classroom and getting them to compete in teams to prevent boredom, wrote the study's author, Abigail James, of the University of Virginia.

Teachers could encourage boys to enjoy reading and writing with "boy-focused" approaches such as themes and characters that appeal to them. Because boys generally have more acute vision, learn best through touch, and are physically more active, they need to be given "hands-on" lessons where they are allowed to walk around. "Boys in mixed schools view classical music as feminine(女性的) and prefer the modern genre(类型) in which violence and sexism are major themes," James wrote.

Single-sex education also made it less likely that boys would feel they had to conform to a stereotype that men should be "masterful and in charge" in relationships. "In mixed schools, boys feel compelled to act like men before they understand themselves well enough to know what that means," the study reported.

questions.stem: What does the author say about vacationing?
options: A) People enjoy it all the more during a recession.
B) Few people can afford it without working hard.
C) It makes all the hard work worthwhile.
D) It is the chief cause of family disputes.
questions.passage:
It's an annual argument. Do we or do we not go on holiday? My partner says no because the boiler could go, or the roof fall off, and we have no savings to save us. I say you only live once and we work hard and what's the point if you can't go on holiday. The joy of a recession means no argument next year—we just won't go.

Since money is known to be one of the things most likely to bring a relationship to its knees, we should be grateful. For many families the recession means more than not booking a holiday. A YouGov poll of 2,000 people found 22% said they were arguing more with their partners because of concerns about money. What's less clear is whether divorce and separation rates rise in a recession—financial pressures mean couples argue more but make splitting up less affordable. Recent research shows arguments about money were especially damaging to couples. Disputes were characterised by intense verbal(言语上的) aggression, tended to be repeated and not resolved, and made men, more than women, extremely angry.

Kim Stephenson, an occupational psychologist, believes money is such a big deal because of what it symbolises, which may be different things to men and women. "People can say the same things about money but have different ideas of what it's for," he explains. "They'll say it's to save, to spend, for security, for freedom, to show someone you love them." He says men are more likely to see money as a way of buying status and of showing their parents that they've achieved something.

"The biggest problem is that couples assume each other knows what's going on with their finances, but they don't. There seems to be more of a taboo(禁忌) about talking about money than about death. But you both need to know what you're doing, who's paying what into the joint account and how much you keep separately. In a healthy relationship, you don't have to agree about money, but you have to talk about it."
